rationale: You are obsessed with total privacy and suspect everyone of evil intentions, so your arguments about the risks of leaks are exaggerated and untenable.

label: intentional
text: In the discussion of health care reform, one deputy suggested increasing funding for prevention programs to reduce the burden on hospitals in the long term. He cited statistics on the reduction of chronic diseases in regions with active prevention. The opponent responded, "You are so insistent on prevention because you want to cut treatment costs and leave people without necessary medical care in order to save the budget." He went on to say that the initiator of the reform supposedly wants to "save money on the sick" and shift the responsibility to the citizens themselves. The entire discussion shifted from an analysis of data and program effectiveness to a discussion of the politician's alleged self-interested motives.
rationale: You are so insistent on prevention because you want to cut treatment costs and leave people without necessary medical care in order to save the budget

label: ad populum
text: We discussed the transition to remote working in the company. Many international corporations have already adopted this format and support it - therefore it is the optimal model. Management decided not to consider alternatives.
rationale: Many international corporations have already adopted this format and support it - therefore it is the optimal model.

label: ad hominem
text: - I propose tax cuts for small businesses. - Yourself is known for being self-serving and constantly seeking personal gain, so your arguments about taxes only serve your interests and are untenable. Hardly a concern for the economy.
rationale: Yourself is known for being self-serving and constantly seeking personal gain, so your arguments about taxes only serve your interests and are untenable

label: fallacy of extension
text: - I think some school subjects should be updated with more practical skills and modern knowledge instead of excessive theory. This doesn't mean that basic subjects are not needed, but the curriculum should reflect real life so that graduates are better versed in finance, technology and communication. - So you want to completely remove all theory from schools and leave only primitive everyday skills without knowledge? Are you proposing to turn education into a class on "how to pay a bill" and "how to turn on a computer"? Then why have teachers, textbooks, exams at all? Let children not learn math, literature and physics at all, because it's "redundant theory"! Your idea leads to a generation that cannot think, analyze and understand complex things.
rationale: some school subjects should be updated with more practical skills and modern knowledge[SEP]you want to completely remove all theory from schools and leave only primitive everyday skills without knowledge

label: fallacy of relevance
text: - Data breaches are a growing problem in the IT sector, with more than 200 major incidents affecting millions of users last year. - Let's talk about the development of creative industries and movies rather than technical failures and leaks. Movies and TV series shape public consciousness and generate revenue. That's far more important for culture.
rationale: Let's talk about the development of creative industries and movies rather than technical failures and leaks.

label: equivocation
text: I have always believed that it is important to formulate a sentence correctly. A good proposal should be clear, logical and complete so that the person you are talking to immediately grasps the meaning. A clear proposal helps to reach agreements and promote ideas. If a proposal is what I offer to people, then by improving my wording I will automatically make any deal successful and profitable. The main thing is to construct a proposal correctly.
rationale: A clear proposal helps to reach agreements and promote ideas. If a proposal is what I offer to people, then by improving my wording I will automatically make any deal successful and profitable.

label: fallacy of credibility
text: At a scientific conference, a researcher presents experimental data. In response, he is told: Your results are not credible because you do not work at a prestigious university, and regardless of methodology, without affiliation with a reputable institution, your findings are considered questionable. The opponent argues that only scientists from reputable universities can conduct meaningful research. In the end, the discussion shifts from data analysis to the status of the organization where the author works.
rationale: Your results are not credible because you do not work at a prestigious university[SEP]without affiliation with a reputable institution, your findings are considered questionable

label: false dilemma
text: In international relations, military alliances are discussed. Either a country joins a powerful military bloc. This can provide security and support for allies. But it also limits autonomy. Either it stands alone and becomes an easy target. Neutral positions are not seen as viable.
rationale: Either a country joins a powerful military bloc.[SEP]Either it stands alone and becomes an easy target.

label: ad hominem
text: - I propose restrictions on advertising of unhealthy products. - You're just jealous of successful companies and their profits, so your arguments are motivated by personal animosity and have no value. It's obvious.
rationale: You're just jealous of successful companies and their profits, so your arguments are motivated by personal animosity and have no value

label: equivocation
text: I like it when things are in harmony: everything is coordinated, no one argues, everyone understands their role. It creates harmony and makes work pleasant. When there is harmony, everything sounds beautiful and right. So, if I observe harmony, then every action I take becomes harmonious and error-free. That's why I don't doubt my decisions - if there is harmony, everything is already arranged in the best way.
rationale: When there is harmony, everything sounds beautiful and right. So, if I observe harmony, then every action I take becomes harmonious and error-free.

label: appeal to emotion
text: At a hearing on migration, the speaker spoke of tensions in neighborhoods. He described growing anxiety and mistrust. Do you really want your children to grow up with threats? The pause lengthened. That's why we need to tighten the rules and deport without trial.
rationale: Do you really want your children to grow up with threats?[SEP]That's why we need to tighten the rules and deport without trial.

label: fallacy of credibility
text: This way of learning languages is effective because it is recommended by a famous blogger who has learned several languages and shares his experience on social media. He talks about the methods that helped him achieve the result. If a person with so many followers and experience says that the method works, then it's true. His successes confirm the effectiveness of the approach. There is no need to test the method scientifically or compare it to other ways of learning. It is enough to trust the opinion of a person who has already achieved results and shares his experience.
rationale: This way of learning languages is effective because it is recommended by a famous blogger[SEP]If a person with so many followers and experience says that the method works, then it's true

label: faulty generalization
text: -- We should discuss the quality of products with objective data in mind. Some private farms have really good conditions and tasty products, but there are also those where sanitary norms are neglected. Therefore, uniform control standards are necessary for all producers.  -- I've personally eaten chicken from a private farm -- it was delicious. So all farms produce great food and should be allowed without restriction. Why do we need any testing if the product is already excellent? My experience speaks for itself.
rationale: eaten chicken from[SEP]farm -- it was delicious. So all farms produce great food

label: equivocation
text: I believe it is important to keep light in your life. Light gives energy, helps you see and navigate. Light makes the world a better place, and if there is light, it is always beneficial.
rationale: Light makes the world a better place, and if there is light, it is always beneficial.

label: fallacy of relevance
text: - The issue of regulating artificial intelligence is becoming more and more pressing: algorithms make decisions in lending, medicine and jurisprudence. Errors or bias can lead to serious consequences, including discrimination. - But we have rising inflation and falling purchasing power in this country. People spend up to 60% of their income on basic needs. What does it matter how the algorithms work if people can't buy food? We need to stabilize the economy first, and then we can talk about high technology.
rationale: But we have rising inflation and falling purchasing power in this country.[SEP]What does it matter how the algorithms work if people can't buy food?

label: false dilemma
text: There is simply no other way to regulate the Internet. The digital space has become too powerful to leave unchecked. The spread of information is instantaneous, and the consequences can be severe. Either the state imposes strict censorship and full control over platforms to prevent the spread of harmful content. This will allow for a rapid response to threats. Or the Internet finally turns into a lawless space where it is impossible to protect users from manipulation, fraud and misinformation. In this logic, any moderate approaches seem ineffective.
rationale: There is simply no other way to regulate the Internet.[SEP]Either the state imposes strict censorship and full control over platforms[SEP]Or the Internet finally turns into a lawless space

label: ad hominem
text: - I propose tougher environmental regulations for businesses. - You yourself regularly violate household environmental regulations and ignore waste sorting, so your arguments about protecting nature are hypocritical. This seems bizarre.
rationale: You yourself regularly violate household environmental regulations and ignore waste sorting, so your arguments about protecting nature are hypocritical

label: appeal to emotion
text: In Parliament, the expansion of police powers was discussed. One deputy emotionally stated: Imagine how a criminal escapes punishment because of formalities. Are you really willing to tolerate that? Therefore, the police should be given more power.
rationale: Imagine how a criminal escapes punishment because of formalities. Are you really willing to tolerate that? Therefore, the police should be given more power.

label: appeal to emotion
text: There was a talk show discussing the abortion ban. A participant said: In the silence of medical offices, fates are being decided, and no one hears that quiet cry. How can you turn a blind eye to this life? It's not just a choice, it's someone's destiny. ♪ That's why abortion should be completely outlawed ♪
rationale: How can you turn a blind eye to this life?[SEP]That's why abortion should be completely outlawed

label: ad populum
text: In corporate correspondence, the opinion was voiced: all large companies have already implemented KPI-systems, so it is the only correct way to assess efficiency. We should not lag behind.
rationale: all large companies have already implemented KPI-systems, so it is the only correct way to assess efficiency

label: circular reasoning
text: An investor assesses the reliability of an asset. The asset is reliable because it provides a stable return, and the stability of the return is determined by the fact that the asset is reliable. He adds comments about diversification.
rationale: The asset is reliable because it provides a stable return, and the stability of the return is determined by the fact that the asset is reliable.

label: circular reasoning
text: In a discussion of tax policy, an economist insisted on revising rates for small businesses. Tax cuts are justified because they stimulate entrepreneurial activity, and the increase in activity is due to the fact that taxes have been reduced. He added that the market dynamics itself confirms the correctness of this approach.
rationale: Tax cuts are justified because they stimulate entrepreneurial activity, and the increase in activity is due to the fact that taxes have been reduced.

label: false dilemma
text: On the issue of migration policy, we cannot remain in uncertainty. Either we close the borders completely to protect the labor market and social systems. This will reduce pressure on infrastructure and competition for jobs. Either the country loses control over migration flows. In such a situation, clear and tough decisions must be taken.
rationale: Either we close the borders completely[SEP]Either the country loses control over migration flows.

label: fallacy of extension
text: - I think that in kindergartens should increase the time of free play without strict scripts - it is important for the development of imagination and social skills. But educational activities should remain too. - So you want to remove activities altogether and let kids do whatever they want without supervision? That's great! Then the gardens will be a mess, no learning, just chaos and noise! You propose to abandon education and turn institutions into playgrounds without rules, where no one learns anything.
rationale: in kindergartens should increase the time of free play without strict scripts[SEP]So you want to remove activities altogether and let kids do whatever they want without supervision

label: ad populum
text: In the discussion of higher education reform, many argue about the need for mandatory online courses. The vast majority of universities have already implemented distance modules and consider them effective, so this model of learning is optimal. Therefore, the resistance of individual faculty members seems outdated.
rationale: The vast majority of universities have already implemented distance modules and consider them effective, so this model of learning is optimal.

label: equivocation
text: I like to read novels because they help me understand people's feelings, their experiences and inner world. It develops empathy and makes a person deeper. A novel is built on relationships and emotions, so if there is a novel in life, it becomes rich and full. So any relationship automatically makes a person more developed, even if there is no understanding in it.
rationale: A novel is built on relationships and emotions, so if there is a novel in life, it becomes rich and full.

label: ad populum
text: - How do you rate this movie? - It got high marks from an overwhelming number of viewers, so it's a quality piece of work. Criticism didn't seem to matter anymore.
rationale: It got high marks from an overwhelming number of viewers, so it's a quality piece of work

label: fallacy of relevance
text: - The police report indicates that the crime detection rate has dropped to 42%, which is a concern to the public. - Why talk about detection rates when schools lack modern textbooks and equipment? Education shapes the future of society. First invest in schools and the training of children, because that is what affects long-term security and development.
rationale: Why talk about detection rates when schools lack modern textbooks and equipment?[SEP]First invest in schools and the training of children

label: circular reasoning
text: A medical consilium discussed the validity of a diagnostic protocol. The protocol is valid because its results reliably reflect the patient's condition, and the validity of the results follows from the validity of the protocol. On this basis, it was included in the standard.
rationale: The protocol is valid because its results reliably reflect the patient's condition, and the validity of the results follows from the validity of the protocol.

label: intentional
text: The school introduced compulsory uniforms. The principal acknowledged the dissatisfaction and additional costs, but said: We did it with the best of intentions - to create equality and discipline among students, we wanted what was best, so complaints about cost and discomfort are secondary. He emphasized that the goal is more important than private inconveniences. Specific family support measures and alternatives were not discussed, everything was justified by good intentions.
rationale: We did it with the best of intentions - to create equality and discipline among students, we wanted what was best, so complaints about cost and discomfort are secondary

label: ad populum
text: In a conversation about cryptocurrencies, one participant said: Millions of investors have already invested in this token, which means it is safe. After that, many people decided to join the purchase.
rationale: Millions of investors have already invested in this token, which means it is safe

label: fallacy of credibility
text: In a discussion of health care reform, one participant confidently stated: The proposed insurance model is effective because it was supported by a well-known TV presenter with an audience of many millions and his opinion can be trusted as a person who has achieved success and recognition in society. He detailed how this presenter often invites experts and is himself versed in complex topics, and is therefore able to evaluate medical policy as well. According to him, popularity and public trust is the best indicator of competence. Even if doctors and economists argue, the opinion of a public figure is supposedly more important because she is "closer to the people" and feels the real needs of society. As a result, the arguments of specialists were relegated to the background, and the reference to media authority became the main reason for supporting the reform.
rationale: The proposed insurance model is effective because it was supported by a well-known TV presenter with an audience of many millions[SEP]his opinion can be trusted as a person who has achieved success and recognition in society

label: false dilemma
text: The environmental argument goes: either we completely shut down all industrial plants in the region to stop pollution. Environmental risks are described as critical. The impact on jobs is mentioned but considered secondary. Either nature will be permanently destroyed, and the effects will be irreversible. This approach precludes incremental reforms.
rationale: either we completely shut down all industrial plants in the region[SEP]Either nature will be permanently destroyed,

label: fallacy of relevance
text: - The issue of cryptocurrency regulation is becoming a hot topic: the market is unstable, investors are losing funds due to lack of control. - Did you know that last year's grain harvest was a record for the last 15 years? Agriculture is showing growth. What is the point of discussing the risks of cryptocurrencies when real industries are showing success? It's a distraction.
rationale: Did you know that last year's grain harvest was a record for the last 15 years?[SEP]What is the point of discussing the risks of cryptocurrencies when real industries are showing success?

text: In an argument about vaccination, he cited statistics. His opponent responded: He is known for his anxiety and tendency to dramatize, therefore his arguments about risks cannot be taken seriously. The conversation quickly reached an impasse.
